transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, I'm here because... things have just been really off lately. Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I've just been, I don't know, snapping at my wife over every little thing around the house. And I'm putting off all my jobs and paperwork that I usually stay on top of without any issue. It's just... I can't seem to get my head quiet. Even when I go out to the workshop or try to get some fishing in, my mind is just racing. I just can't seem to settle down.
When did you first notice these feelings of irritability and racing thoughts start, in relation to when your father-in-law moved in?

Well, he had a fall, and that's why he had to move in with us. I'd say it was within the first couple of months after he got here. That's when I noticed I was already falling behind on my paperwork, and... well, arguing with my wife over all the household changes we had to make. It just started up pretty quickly after he arrived.
Besides feeling irritable and on edge, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy since your father-in-law moved in?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. It's more just... frustration, I guess. And it's not that I've lost interest in fishing or being out in the workshop—I still want to do those things. It's just that when I try, I can't seem to turn my brain off enough to actually enjoy them right now.

Do you find yourself worrying excessively about other areas of your life too—like work, health, or finances—or does the racing, worried feeling seem to be specifically about the changes since your father-in-law moved in?

No, it's really just about the situation at home. Work and finances and all that... they're fine, I'm not worried about them. It's just... ever since he moved in, the house feels different, the routine is gone, and that's what's got my mind spinning all the time. I'm not sitting around worrying about my health or anything like that. It's just the changes here at the house.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed irritability, difficulty relaxing, racing thoughts, and impaired functioning (falling behind on paperwork, marital conflict) within two months of a clearly identifiable psychosocial stressor (father-in-law moving in after a fall). Symptoms are disproportionate to the stressor and out of character, but do not meet full criteria for a depressive episode (no sadness, no anhedonia) or generalized anxiety disorder (worry is restricted to the specific situational stressor rather than multiple life domains). This pattern—stressor-related emotional and behavioral symptoms with functional impairment, predominantly anxious in quality, following a distinct stressor—is most consistent with Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety (F43.22).
